newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance firms sign pact to seek bank licence.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance firms sign pact to seek bank licence.

text.p: Seven Thai brokerages signed a memorandum of understanding to apply jointly for a commercial banking licence, they said in statements on Wednesday.

The firms were Nava Finance and Securities Plc, Thaimex Finance and Securities Plc, CMIC Finance and Securities Plc, Thai Thanakorn Finance Plc and unlisted Thanapol Finance and Securities Plc, Thanasap Finance and Securities Plc and Bangkok Asian Finance Plc.

"The objective is to merge operations to apply for a commercial banking licence in which NAVA, CMIC and TMF will be the group leaders," CMIC Finance and Securities Plc said in a statement issued to the Stock Exchange of Thailand.
The group leaders had earlier this month announced plans to merge. The deal is expected to be completed by the end of 1997.
CMIC's statement said the group's total assets, as of December 1996 were 190.4 billion baht ($7.3 billion) with share capital worth 21.1 billion baht ($815 million).
The central Bank of Thailand has encouraged consolidation among Thailand's finance and securities companies, and offered merging firms the chance to apply for a new commercial banking licence.
